Title:                        Zoning Reclassification Map No. 3-G at 1402 W Chestnut St
                              - App No. 20876
Committee(s) Assignment:      Committee on Zoning, Landmarks and Building Standards
                               ORDINANCE

BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CHICAGO:


SECTION 1. Title 17 of the Municipal Code of Chicago, the Chicago Zoning Ordinance

be amended by changing all the RS3 Residential Single-Unit (Detached House) District

symbols and indications as shown on Map No. 3-G in the area bounded by


       The alley next north of and parallel to West Chestnut Street; a line 24 feet
       west of and parallel to North Noble Street; West Chestnut Street; and a
       line 48 feet west of and parallel to North Noble Street,


to those of a RM4.5 Residential Multi-Unit District.


SECTION 2. This ordinance shall be in force and effect from and afi:er its passage and

due publication.




Common Address of Property:          1402 West Chestnut Street

9.    Present Zoning District: RS-3                   Proposed Zoning District: RM-4.5

10.   Lot size in square feet (or dimensions): 3,084 square feet

11.   Current Use of the Property: The subject property is improved with a two-story residential
      building.

12.   Reason for rezoning the property: The Applicant is proposing develop the property with a
      new four-story residential building that will contain three (3) dwelling units.

13.   Describe the proposed use of the property after the rezoning. Indicate the number of
      dwelling unit number of parking spaces; approximate square footage of any commercial
      space; and height of the proposed building. (BE SPECIFIC): The Applicant is proposing
      develop the property with a new four-story residential building that will contain three (3)
      dwelling units. The proposed building will be masonry in construction and measure 44
      feet-11 inches in height. The residential building will be supported by three (3) surface
      parking spaces located at the rear of the subject lot.

14.   The Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) requires on-site affordable housing units
      and/or a financial contribution for residential housing projects with ten or more units that
      receive a zoning change which, among other triggers, increases the allowable floor area,
      or, for existing Planned Developments, increases the number of units (see attached fact
      sheet or visit vyww.cityofchicago.org/ARO for more information). Is this project subject to
